rationale: C20 supplies a particularly close drafting template: both memoranda describe a private bill excusing a named person's failure to meet a statutory filing deadline, recount the agency record concerning the late filing, emphasize unequal treatment of others subject to the same general law, and reject relief because it would create an undesirable precedent. C22 and C01 share the same special-relief and expired-deadline framework, but their language and operative sequence are less closely aligned with the child.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Essentially, H. R. 1733 would waive this requirement for the named taxpayers.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The bill would permit the payment ... without regard to the statutory limitation on the period within which an application for such payment may be filed.
shared_material.explanation: Both characterize the private bill as an exemption for named persons from a mandatory statutory filing deadline.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The records of the Treasury Department disclose that it was not involved in the untimely filing by these taxpayers.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: there are no records of such calls in the Social Security Administration files. In view of her failure to file application ... within the time fixed by law
shared_material.explanation: Both use the responsible agency's records to establish that the claimant missed the deadline without a documented governmental basis for excusing it.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The granting of special relief in this case would constitute an unfair discrimination against other taxpayers similarly situated
shared_material.parent_excerpt: This bill would provide special relief permitting one individual to receive a social insurance benefit under conditions identical with those under which ... the same benefit must be denied to others similarly situated.
shared_material.explanation: This is a distinctive shared equity rationale centered on discriminatory private relief for one late filer over similarly situated persons.

shared_material.child_excerpt: would create an undesirable precedent which might encourage other taxpayers to seek relief in the same manner.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: enactment of S. 277 would establish for the Social Security Program an undesirable precedent which until now has been avoided.
shared_material.explanation: Both make the precedent created by case-specific waiver of a filing deadline an express ground for withholding approval.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Under the circumstances, therefore, I am constrained to withhold my approval of the bill.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I am reluctant to deny relief in a case of this kind, but there are at least two persuasive considerations which compel me to withhold my approval
shared_material.explanation: The conclusions use closely related withholding language following the same deadline, equal-treatment, and precedent analysis.
